title: Singapore's Reliance on Nurses from Philippines and Impact on Local Nursing Workforce Numbers Following Recent Suspension
what_it_is: Singapore's Reliance on Nurses from Philippines and Impact on Local Nursing Workforce Numbers Following Recent Suspension

sections.label: Philippines suspension, nursing workforce
sections.summary: MOH monitors the Philippines' permit suspension, works with employers on nursing workforce adequacy, and urges diversified recruitment as local registrations rose.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) is closely monitoring the impact of the Philippines’ suspension of permits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We are working with healthcare employers to ensure the adequacy and sustainability of our nursing workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Healthcare employers should also diversify their recruitment sources.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In 2020, there were around 1,400 new registrations from locals, compared to around 1,200 in 2019.

sections.label: Singapore registered nurse stock
sections.summary: Singapore's registered nurse stock rose about 19% from 36,000 in 2013 to over 42,000 in 2019, almost 7.5 per 1,000 population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For the second question on how we can ramp up our local supply of nurses, Singapore's stock of registered nurses increased by about 19% from 36,000 in 2013, to more than 42,000 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This translates to almost 7.5 registered nurses per 1,000 population, which is a good number compared to many other Asian economies like Hong Kong and Taiwan.

sections.label: Public healthcare nurses' salary increase
sections.summary: Public sector healthcare nurses will receive about a 5% to 14% increase in monthly base salaries from July this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Public sector healthcare nurses will have an increase of about 5% to 14% in their monthly base salaries from July this year.

sections.label: E-rostering across public health clusters
sections.summary: E-rostering will be scaled across the public health clusters by the end of 2021 to facilitate scheduling of work shifts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To facilitate the scheduling of work shifts, e-rostering will be scaled across the public health clusters by the end of 2021.
